newsitem.title: USA: SOCCER-COLORADO WINS TWICE TO MOVE INTO SECOND PLACE.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-COLORADO WINS TWICE TO MOVE INTO SECOND PLACE.

text.p: The Colorado Rapids completed a memorable weekend Sunday by winning their second road game in 48 hours with a 2-0 victory over the Columbus Crew in Major League Soccer action.
Paul Bravo and former U.S. international Roy Wegerle scored for the Rapids (7-8), who moved into second place in the Western Conference as they rebounded from a 5-0 defeat by D.C. United last week.
Goalkeeper Marcus Hahnemann made four saves en route to his fourth shutout as the slumping Crew (6-8) lost for the sixth successive time.
On Friday, former MetroStars captain Peter Vermes, who joined Colorado in a pre-season trade, scored the go-ahead go against his ex-team as the Rapids registered a 3-1 win in East Rutherford, N.J.
Rookie Ross Paule scored his first goal and set up Sean Henderson's goal. Venezuelan Giovanni Savarese scored his sixth goal for the MetroStars, who fell to 5-9.
The MetroStars, directed by World Cup champion coach Carlos Alberto Parreira of Brazil, experienced a miserable weekend, dropping a 3-1 decision to the Dallas Burn (8-6) in Dallas on Sunday.
Mexican Damian Alvarez, Dante Washington and Jason Kreis scored for the Burn, while Miles Joseph produced the MetroStars' lone goal.
In Foxboro, defending MLS champion D.C. United (11-3), the Eastern Conference leaders, won its sixth consecutive game by edging New England 1-0 to drop the Revolution to 10-4.
Tony Sanneh scored in the 72nd minute against former Italian international goalkeeper Walter Zenga.

In Kansas City, Ronald Cerritos scored twice and U.S. National Team striker Eric Wynalda set up all three goals as the San Jose Clash (5-9) snapped a five-game losing streak with a 3-1 win over the Kansas City Wizards (8-5).
Chris Sullivan also tallied for the Clash. Sean Bowers scored for the Wizards, who remained atop the Western Conference.
In Pasadena, the Los Angeles Galaxy (4-9), in its first game under interim coach Octavio Zambrano, finally got the offence going and stunned the Tampa Bay Mutiny (6-7) with a 4-1 triumph.
Guatemalan Martin Machon, El Salvadoran international Mauricio Cienfuegos, Cobi Jones and Greg Vanney scored for Los Angeles, which had a league-low nine goals entering the match.
Zambrano replaced Lothar Osiander, who was fired earlier in the week.
